newsitem.title: UK: TOP ENGLISH SOCCER CLUBS MULL OWN TV SERVICE - FT.
newsitem.headline: TOP ENGLISH SOCCER CLUBS MULL OWN TV SERVICE - FT.

text.p: England's top soccer clubs have been advised to set up their own television service when a deal with satellite broadcaster BSkyB expires in 2001, the Financial Times said on Tuesday.

The newspaper said an interim report prepared for Premier League clubs had calculated top soccer would be worth 1.3 billion pounds ($2.2 billion) to BSkyB over the next four years, twice the 670 million pounds it was paying to show live Premiership soccer over this period.

The report said that if the league was to benefit fully from its popularity it should consider setting up a dedicated pay-TV service in 2001 and receive all the revenues generated by coverage of matches, instead of sharing them with BSkyB. ($ = 0.604 British Pounds)
